title: Software Incompatibility With Vehicle Immobilizer Control Module
plain: The software in the immobilizer module does not match what the other modules expect. This usually happens after a module was replaced, swapped from another vehicle or updated.
symptoms: Security light on or flashing
Car may crank but not start

causes.name: Module replaced with a used or wrong part number
Module not programmed, or programmed with the wrong software
Software update interrupted, for example by low battery voltage
Other modules need updating to match

checks: Ask whether any module was recently replaced or reprogrammed
Check the module part number and software level against the maker data
Keep a battery maintainer connected during any reprogramming
fix: Program the module with the correct software using dealer-level tools.

title: Invalid Data Received
plain: A module received a message over the vehicle network that it could not use because the data was out of range or did not make sense.
symptoms: Warning light on
Features that depend on the bad message may not work

causes.name: Faulty sensor feeding another module
Module software that needs an update
Low battery voltage
Network wiring problem

checks: Scan all modules to find which one is sending bad data
Test the battery and grounds
fix: Find the module or sensor sending bad data and repair or update it.

title: Invalid Data Received From ECM/PCM "A"
plain: Another module received a message from the engine computer (ECM/PCM) that does not make sense, such as a value that is out of range or does not add up. It runs the engine, so other modules rely on it for engine speed, temperature and other data.
symptoms: Check engine light and several other warning lights on
Car may not start, or may stall
Gauges such as the tachometer may stop working

causes.name: A faulty engine sensor (such as throttle or pedal position) giving the engine computer bad data
The engine computer (ECM/PCM) needs a software update
Low battery voltage or poor ground causing bad messages
Network wiring problem or interference
Failed engine computer (ECM/PCM)

checks: Check the engine computer (ECM/PCM) for its own stored codes and fix those first
Test the battery and grounds
Check for software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix any fault in the engine computer (ECM/PCM) or its sensors, then update the software if needed.

cost.job: Diagnose engine computer data fault and update software

drive: Use care. Bad data from the engine computer can cause stalling, a no-start or odd transmission behavior. If it stalls or several warnings come on, have it towed. If it runs normally, get it checked soon.
test_first: Read codes in the engine computer first, since it may be reporting a sensor fault, then check its power, grounds and network wiring, and look for software updates before replacing modules.
